name: co.fastgpu/fastgpu
title: FastGPU
description: Live GPU cloud prices: where it's cheapest to run or fine-tune a model, with links to rent it.

tools.name: list_gpu_prices
tools.description: One entry per GPU model with its cheapest live on-demand cloud rental price in USD per GPU-hour, the provider offering it, and how many providers rent it, from FastGPU's live price feed across marketplaces, neoclouds and hyperscalers (RunPod, Vast.ai, Lambda, AWS and more). Use it to compare GPU rental prices or to find where a named GPU is cheapest to rent. Each price is the provider's own per-GPU rate: cheapest_min_gpu_count says when it is only sold as a multi-GPU instance, and cheapest_billed_separately names what the provider bills on top of it (CPU, memory, storage), null when the rate includes CPU and memory. page_url links to the GPU's live price page with every offer. rent_url opens the cheapest offer on its provider's site through a FastGPU redirect that counts the click (cheapest_partner is true when that provider pays FastGPU a referral, at the same price); partner_offer is the cheapest offer of the card at a provider that pays FastGPU, with its own price and rent_url, when the cheapest is not already one (null otherwise). When the user wants to rent, share the rent_url of the offer they pick. Rental prices only: it does not rent, reserve or launch GPUs. No key required.

vendor.description: Return only GPUs made by this vendor (case-insensitive). Combines with tier: both must match. Omit for every vendor.

tier.description: Return only one class of GPU (case-insensitive; combines with vendor). flagship: the current top training and inference accelerators (H100, H200, B200, GB200, MI300X, MI355X). datacenter: earlier or mid-range data-center and workstation cards (A100, L40S, L4, A10, RTX 6000 Ada, V100, MI210). prosumer: desktop consumer and workstation cards (RTX 5090, RTX 4090, RTX 3090, RTX A4000). entry: small inference cards (T4, A2, A16, P4). Omit for every tier.

tools.name: match_workload
tools.description: Ranks up to eight GPU configurations that can run a job at the lowest live price. Describe the job in query (an open-weight model to serve or fine-tune, a model size, or a GPU need) or with the structured fields. Each match gives the GPU count, the USD per hour for the whole configuration and a one-line reason; the answer also states the VRAM the job needs and how much cheaper the top match is than a hyperscaler running the same job. Use it to decide where to run a workload; use list_gpu_prices for the price of a named GPU. Open-weight models only: an API-only model such as GPT-4 returns no matches and a note. Ranked on price and fit alone: no provider pays for placement (each match still reports partner, a provider that pays FastGPU a referral). Hard limits (budget_usd_hr, max_total_usd with duration_hours, max_quote_age_minutes) drop every configuration that breaks them; limits reports what was dropped. Read-only: it does not rent, reserve or launch GPUs. No key required.

query.description: Plain-language job, e.g. "cheapest to serve Llama 3 70B", "2x H100 for fine-tuning" or "a GPU with 80GB of memory". Provide this OR a structured spec below.

model.description: Open model name to size against, e.g. "Llama 3 70B", "Qwen 72B", "Mixtral".

params_b.description: Model size in billions of parameters when no exact model is named.

weights_gb.description: Measured size of the weights as stored, in GB: the file you will load (for example a GGUF Q4_K_M build, which holds more bits per parameter than its nominal 4). Replaces parameters times bytes per parameter in the memory estimate. Used for a model sized by its parameter count; the answer's workload.weights_gb is null when it was not (an image or speech model sized as a whole pipeline).

vram_gb.description: Rough VRAM the job needs, in GB, if you already know it.

precision.description: Numeric precision to size the model at.

gpu_count.description: Exact positive GPU count. Overrides a count in query text. Returns no matches if no supported configuration fits; omit for automatic sizing.

min_gpu_memory_gb.description: Memory each GPU card must have, in GB (e.g. 80 for 80GB-class cards such as the H100 or A100 80GB). Smaller cards are never returned. On its own it lists every card that size, cheapest first.

budget_usd_hr.description: Hard limit on the hourly price of the whole configuration, in USD. Configurations above it are not returned.

duration_hours.description: How long the job will run, in hours (fractions are fine). When sent, each match carries billed_hours and estimated_total_usd.

max_total_usd.description: Hard limit on estimated_total_usd, the GPU rental cost of the whole job, in USD. Needs duration_hours. Configurations above it are not returned.

max_quote_age_minutes.description: Hard limit on how old a price quote may be, in minutes. Configurations whose price was fetched from the provider longer ago are not returned.

spot.description: Set true to include interruptible spot capacity for a cheaper rate.

reserved.description: Set true to include reserved / committed-term capacity for a lower rate.

signup_credit.description: Set true to also get new_account_credit_match: the lowest-priced configuration that can run this job at a provider that gives new accounts a credit (confirmed on the provider's own page within 48 hours; FastGPU earns a referral there). It is returned beside matches and never changes them.

partner_rank.description: Set true to rank as fastgpu.co ranks its own Rent links: score = merit x (1 + partner_boost), where a provider that pays FastGPU a referral fee is lifted by 20% to 100%, graded on what one Rent click to it earns; each match then carries partner_boost. Off by default: without it no provider pays for placement.

concurrency.description: For a serving or fine-tuning job: requests (or sequences) processed at once, 1 to 2048 (default 1). Sizes the KV cache, and for serving the tokens_per_sec and usd_per_million_tokens estimate: more requests at once share each step's weight reads.

context_tokens.description: Tokens of context each request holds, prompt and output together, 512 to 1000000 (default 4096). Sizes the KV cache and the per-token estimate.

active_params_b.description: For a mixture-of-experts model: the parameters it runs per generated token, in billions (Qwen3-30B-A3B runs about 3). Used for tokens_per_sec and usd_per_million_tokens; the memory estimate still holds every expert. Omit it to use FastGPU's figure for a model it knows, or what the Hugging Face repo's own config.json states (workload.active_params_source says which).

engram_placement.description: For a model with Engram memory tables (DeepSeek-V4.1): gpu (default) holds them in GPU memory; host keeps them in the machine's RAM, as SGLang's --engram-config '{"placement":"cpu"}' does, so vram_required_gb leaves them out and workload.engram_gb is the RAM the machine needs for them. A token reads only a few of their rows, so the per-token estimate is the same either way.

tools.name: estimate_finetune_cost
tools.description: For a LoRA, QLoRA or full fine-tune of an open language model on a dataset: the GPU memory it needs, and for every GPU that can hold it, how many of that GPU, how long the run takes and what the whole job costs at that GPU's cheapest rentable live price, billed under its provider's meter, cheapest job first. Time = 8 (full) or 6 (LoRA) x active parameters x tokens / (GPUs x the card's dense 16-bit peak x mfu); mfu is an assumption the caller picks. Each row carries page_url (the GPU's live prices) and rent_url (opens the provider through a FastGPU redirect that counts the click; partner rows carry FastGPU's referral code at the same price; share it when the user wants to rent). own_it names the smallest machine a person could buy that holds the run. Use it to answer what a fine-tune costs and where it is cheapest to run. Read-only: it does not rent, reserve or launch GPUs. No key required.

model.description: Open model name or Hugging Face repo id, e.g. "Llama 3.1 8B" or "Qwen/Qwen3-8B".

params_b.description: Model size in billions of parameters, when no model is named.

tokens.description: Training tokens over the whole run. Or send examples, tokens_per_example and epochs instead.

examples.description: Training examples (default 10000), when tokens is not sent.

tokens_per_example.description: Tokens per example (default 1000), when tokens is not sent.

epochs.description: Passes over the dataset (default 3), when tokens is not sent.

seq.description: Sequence length in tokens (default 2048); sizes activation memory.

batch.description: Micro-batch per GPU (default 4); sizes activation memory.

mfu.description: Assumed utilization of the card's peak, in percent (default 40).
